Manish Kumar 17 Aug 2026 09:47 IST Follow Us Hoymiles Deploys 350 kW String Inverters in Bihar Under PM-KUSUM Photograph: (Hoymiles) Global energy solutions company Hoymiles has commissioned a 7.7 MW solar power project in Gaya, Bihar, deploying 20 units of its 350 kW HINV350HX-G2 string inverters in what the company describes as its first project under the PM-KUSUM initiative in the area. Advertisment The project was executed by Naw Dharam Energy as the EPC partner, while Sun Solista served as the distribution partner for Hoymiles' inverter supply. The plant is set to dispatch green energy from the ground-mounted project to the local grid.. Advertisment The commissioning is significant for Hoymiles' India strategy as the company has traditionally been more closely associated with microinverter technology but has been expanding its portfolio in the country to include utility-scale string inverters, hybrid inverters and battery energy storage systems. 20 string inverters deployed The 7.7 MW project uses 20 HINV350HX-G2 string inverters, each with a rated capacity of 350 kW. According to Hoymiles, the inverter incorporates six 75-amp maximum power point trackers (MPPTs) and is compatible with both 182 mm and 210 mm photovoltaic modules. The company claims a maximum efficiency of 99.05% and European efficiency of 98.8%. Advertisment The HINV350HX-G2 is also designed for outdoor utility-scale applications, with IP66 protection and C5 anti-corrosion capability. The inverter has an SCR of ≥1.1, aimed at supporting stable operation under challenging grid conditions The choice of a 350 kW string inverter platform for the Gaya project reflects the growing deployment of high-capacity string inverters in utility-scale solar, where developers are seeking greater design flexibility while retaining relatively granular power-conversion architecture. Advertisment Hoymiles Expanding Portfolio Hoymiles' expansion in India is increasingly extending into energy storage alongside its established microinverter business. Advertisment In February, the company introduced its HOYDC 5MWh containerised BESS, targeting utility-scale and C&I applications. The system uses liquid cooling, integrated safety systems and a modular architecture designed for applications including renewable-energy integration, peak shaving, load shifting and grid support. The broader portfolio reflects Hoymiles' positioning as a solar and storage technology provider rather than a microinverter-only company. Its product portfolio now spans residential, C&I and utility applications, including microinverters, hybrid inverters and energy-storage solutions. Bihar PM-KUSUM Advertisment Read the Next Article

bihar_raw_news.content: Oswal Pumps Limited has received a letter of award from North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited (NBPDCL) for setting up 20 MW of grid-connected rooftop solar projects for 18,089 consumers in the Darbhanga circle in the state. The projects will be developed under the capital expenditure plus renewable energy service company mode in the utility-led aggregation model of the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG-MBY). Each rooftop solar plant will have a capacity of 1.1 kW, with the total contract valued at approximately Rs 0.78 billion. The projects are to be commissioned within nine months from the execution of the respective power purchase agreements. Furthermore, the scope includes the design, engineering, procurement, manufacturer’s quality assurance and factory testing, transportation, handling, storage, erection, including all civil, structural, electrical and general works, piping, cabling, installation, testing and commissioning. It also covers data acquisition and communication facilities for centralised monitoring, project financing, required permits, sanctions and clearances, and insurance. The scope also covers operation and maintenance of the rooftop solar systems for 10 years from commissioning and supply of the generated solar power to the concerned Bihar discoms. In June 2026, Oswal Pumps secured orders for 63 MW of grid-connected rooftop solar projects in Bihar under the PMSG-MBY. The projects were awarded by NBPDCL and South Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited, covering 57,492 household installations across Motihari, Saharsa and Ara. The orders are valued at approximately Rs 2.47 billion, with an additional estimated long-term revenue potential of Rs 2.57 billion from energy supply over 10 years. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar stampede: Seven killed, 14 injured after barricades collapse near Ashok Dham temple At least six people died in a stampede-like incident at the Ashokdham Temple in Bihar’s Lakhisarai district, police said on Monday, August 17. By CNBCTV18.com August 17, 2026, 2:11:49 PM IST (Updated) 2 Min Read At least seven devotees were killed and 14 others injured in a stampede near the Ashok Dham temple in Bihar’s Lakhisarai district on Monday (August 17) morning, officials said. The incident occurred around 6.30 am at the Ashok Dham halt railway station, a short walk from the temple, where a large number of pilgrims had gathered to offer water to Lord Shiva during the holy month of Shravan. A section of the barricades reportedly gave way under pressure from the crowd, causing devotees to fall over one another, Lakhisarai District Magistrate Shailendra Kumar told PTI. Rescue operations were underway, while the injured were being taken to the nearest government hospital. Authorities were also working to identify the deceased and injured. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary expressed grief over the deaths and announced compensation of ₹4 lakh for the family of each deceased. “The incident at Ashok Dham in Lakhisarai is tragic and heartbreaking,” Choudhary wrote on X, adding that officials had been directed to ensure “proper and prompt medical care” for the injured. President Droupadi Murmu too took to X to condole those to lost their family members to the stampede. "The news of the deaths of devotees in the stampede in Lakhisarai district of Bihar is extremely painful. I express my deepest condolences to the grief-stricken families. He hinted towards Trump saying while Modi was trying to “hug” him, he in return was trying to pull his collar. Later, Dixit made an uncanny remark telling Rahul, “Hope you did not hug me thinking I am Meloni.” Rahul said he would talk about that later, but he never did. bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav announces Raj Bhavan march on 19 August over Bihar paper leaks, Siwan firing
bihar_raw_news.content: Home India Tejashwi Yadav announces Raj Bhavan march on 19 August over Bihar paper... India Tejashwi Yadav announces Raj Bhavan march on 19 August over Bihar paper leaks, Siwan firing Yadav called Bihar the “worst-performing” state when it comes to education, and questioned who ordered the firing during the student protest in Siwan. ANI 16 August, 2026 08:23 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin RJD's Tejashwi Yadav at a press conference in Patna | ANI Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna: Leader of Opposition in the Bihar Assembly and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday launched a scathing attack on the Bihar government, alleging a complete collapse of the examination system and law and order in the state. Announcing a protest march to the Raj Bhavan on August 19, Yadav highlighted the recurring issue of paper leaks and the recent violent incident in Siwan where students were allegedly fired upon. Speaking to reporters in Patna, Tejashwi Yadav said, “There isn’t a single exam or recruitment drive where the paper doesn’t get leaked. Whether it is the Class 10 exam, the Class 12 exam, or a recruitment test, the paper leaks every time, and a fair selection process has never taken place.” Show Full Article The RJD leader further criticized the state’s standing in the education sector, labeling Bihar as the “worst-performing” state. “Bihar is the worst-performing state when it comes to education. You must have seen the incident that occurred in Siwan; an AK-47 was fired. Students are fighting for their rights, yet they are being fired upon. Who ordered the firing? In light of this, we have decided to hold a march to the Raj Bhavan on August 19 and present our grievances to the Governor,” Yadav said. Expressing dissatisfaction over the administrative action taken following the Siwan incident, the former Deputy Chief Minister accused the government of shielding high-ranking officials. “We had met the DGP previously as well, and we had asked the government who was responsible for this. No action has been taken so far. Only a single constable has been dismissed, but there has been no suspension of the SP, nor has any major action been taken. The government is protecting those responsible,” he alleged. Reiterating the party’s plan for a massive demonstration, Yadav added, “On the 19th, we will march to the Raj Bhavan to demand accountability and justice for the students of Bihar.” The remarks came after Bihar’s Siwan witnessed clashes between student protesters and police personnel during protests on July 25 over alleged examination irregularities and the NEET paper leak controversy. Police used tear gas shells and lathi charge to disperse the protesters following reports of stone-pelting. An AK-47 firing incident was also reported during the unrest. Earlier on July 27, speaking to ANI, Yadav also demanded that the Bihar government make public the details of students arrested in connection with the protests, including the charges against them. bihar_raw_news.title: Successful SIR in Bihar led to record turnout in 2025 assembly polls: CEC
bihar_raw_news.content: Agencies Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar Patna : Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Sunday asserted that the "successful" Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar last year had led to a significant rise in voter turnout in the assembly polls that followed. Speaking to reporters at Patna airport, the CEC, who is on a two-day tour of the state, said the voting percentage in the 2025 Bihar assembly polls was higher than turnouts witnessed in advanced countries such as the US, the UK and France. "Bihar is the land where Vaishali, the cradle of democracy, is situated. We take pride in the fact that the SIR was conducted here successfully for the first time," Kumar said. Also Read: Congress' Jairam Ramesh calls Gyanesh Kumar a 'weapon of mass destruction' for electoral rolls The CEC pointed out that following the mammoth exercise, conducted over a three-month period during which around 70 lakh names were knocked off the electoral rolls, a sharp rise was seen in the voter turnout when assembly polls which were held soon afterwards. Live Events "As you all know, men and women came out in large numbers to vote and the turnout broke all records in the state. It may be noted that the voter turnout in Bihar assembly polls was higher than what has been seen, over the years, in major democracies like the US, the UK, France, Spain and Japan," the CEC added. The assembly polls held in November last year registered a voter turnout of 67.25 per cent, which, according to the Election Commission, was the highest for the state since Independence. national_raw_news.content: The entire Union Territory of Ladakh will undergo Population Enumeration, the second phase of Census 2027 in next month, September, with the commencement of Self-Enumeration from today. The Self-Enumeration is scheduled from August 17 to 31 in the Union Territory. The 2027 will complete Ladakh with 1st October as the reference date. Ladakh would become the first Union Territory in the country to complete the Census 2027 exercise, with Population Enumeration scheduled from September 1 to 30. The self-enumeration is beginning today. Around 637 Enumeration Blocks (EBs) would be created for complete coverage of Ladakh. Chief Principal Census Officer and Director of Census Operations for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh Amit Sharma, during a press conference, said the September schedule had been planned in view of the region’s harsh winter conditions, difficult terrain and limited accessibility of Ladakh. Population Enumeration will collect detailed information on population distribution, demographic composition, education, economic activity, migration, disability, language, fertility and other population characteristics. Census 2027 is being conducted digitally, with House Listing Operations completed from June 1 to 30. The first phase achieved 100 per cent digital data collection.

national_raw_news.title: 12 mins ago | National 71 NTA Announces Re-Test for Three UGC-NET June 2026 Papers
national_raw_news.content: The National Testing Agency NTA today announced re-test for three papers of the UGC-NET examination, English, Commerce and Sociology following complaints about several errors in these papers. NTA said, the English paper will be held on 9th September from 9 am to 12 noon in Shift 1, while the Commerce paper will be conducted the same day from 3 pm to 6 pm in Shift 2. The Sociology paper will be held on 10th September from 9 am to 12 noon in Shift 1. The NTA had conducted the UGC-NET June 2026 examination from 22nd to 30th June across 87 subjects for the award of Junior Research Fellowship, eligibility for assistant professor, and admission to PhD programmes. NTA had formed a committee to enquire into and look into these errors. The Committee recommended that, in the interest of holding a fair and error-free examination, these three papers should be re-conducted.

national_raw_news.title: 16 mins ago | Regional News 8 Protesting Jharkhand students to hold fresh round of talks with State Government in Ranchi today
national_raw_news.content: JPSC-JSSC aspirants’ agitation in Jharkhand has entered its 24th day, with students intensifying their protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. A fresh round of talks between the government and student representatives is scheduled for today. JPSC-JSSC aspirants took out a protest march from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to Albert Ekka Chowk in Ranchi yesterday and burnt effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav. The students raised slogans demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Meanwhile, the state government has invited the protesting students for talks today at 2pm in Ranchi, with the students allowed to participate along with their legal advisers. The Reform Manch has said that if the government accepts the students’ demands, steps could be taken towards ending the agitation; otherwise, the protest will continue. The students have already announced a protest outside the Chief Minister’s residence on August 20, but said the final decision would depend on Devendra Nath Mahto’s health and the outcome of today’s talks.

national_raw_news.title: 18 mins ago | Regional News 12 Annual pilgrimage to Himalayan shrine of Budha Amarnath begins in Jammu and Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: The 12-day-long annual Shri Buddha Amarnath Yatra to the ancient Baba Budha Amarnath Temple in Rajpura village of Mandi Tehsil in Poonch district commences today amid tight security arrangements. The Yatra will continue until August 28 and will culminate on Raksha Bandhan. Authorities have enforced strict multi-tier security and surveillance across Rajouri, Poonch, and transit routes. The Hindu pilgrimage is held annually during the auspicious monsoon month of Shravan to the ancient Baba Budha Amarnath Temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located in Rajpura village in Mandi Tehsil of Poonch district. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha today flagged off the first batch of the Yatris from the Bhagwati Nagar Yatri Niwas in Jammu toward the border district of Poonch in the morning under tight security arrangements. Strict multi-tier security and surveillance have been enforced along the transit routes across the twin border districts of Rajouri and Poonch with the units of Special Operations Group of J&K Police conducting search and verification operations near lodging sites like Dashnami Akhara. The convoys of the devotees will move under police escort, with additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) deployed. Traffic Police issued a strict advisory with mandatory cut-off times for registered pilgrim convoys travelling along the Jammu-Poonch route from today to August 28. District administration and local bodies have finalised arrangements, including waterproof tents, community kitchen (Langar) locations, parking layouts, and health care stations along the pilgrimage route. Langars and reception counters have been set up at vital transit locations like Sunderbani, Nowshera, and Rajal in Rajouri district. The Poonch district administration has launched a dedicated portal to facilitate advance registration for the pilgrims coming from across the country. The journey traditionally commences from the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu, taking the pilgrims about 230 km northwest into the mountainous terrain of Poonch where the Budha Amarnath shrine sits 4 thousand 600 feet above the sea level and features a self-manifested white stone Shivling. Devotees traditionally bathe in the nearby holy Pulastya River (named after Rishi Pulastya) before entering the temple for prayers. Many believe completing this yatra adds profound completeness to a devotee’s broader pilgrimage path to the higher-altitude Amarnath Cave shrine. For assistance, pilgrims may contact Traffic Control Unit (TCU) Jammu at 0191-2467302, TCU Srinagar at 0194-2479871, or email igtraffic@jkpolice.gov.in.

national_raw_news.title: India to host 12th BRICS Environment Ministers Meeting in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: India will host the twelfth BRICS Environment Ministers Meeting in New Delhi tomorrow. This meeting will be preceded by the BRICS Senior Officers’ Meeting of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development. The event will be held under the overarching theme of India’s BRICS Chairship 2026 – Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The BRICS Environment Ministers’ Meeting would be presided over by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said that the meeting will provide a platform to engage in substantive discussions, foster consensus, and strengthen environmental cooperation. The Ministry further said that as part of the Chairship, India has identified four priority areas for focused engagements under the BRICS Environment Working Group. The priority areas are Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles, Afforestation, Forest Fire Management and Disaster Resilience, Circular Economy, and Adaptation.

national_raw_news.title: MoS Dr Jitendra Singh to Confer National Anubhav Awards 2026 in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr Jitendra Singh, will confer the National Anubhav Awards, 2026, today in New Delhi. The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions said, the event will also feature the release of the Handbook on Pension Mitra, and Guidelines for the Nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign-Five. It also said that a Bank Exhibition will also be organised as part of the programme, where 17 Pension Disbursing Banks will showcase their products and services designed for the retiring employees. For the National Anubhav Awards Scheme, 2026, the 15 selected awardees have contributed to nation-building and have been part of various ambitious projects of the Government like, Passport Seva Kendra, the repealing of old rules and formulation of new rules, suiting the current scenario, Technological adaptation in the administration and accounting, energy conservation, etc. The ‘Anubhav’ platform provides a forum for retiring/retired employees of Central Government employees, 12 Public Sector Banks and Central Public Sector Enterprises to share their experiences of working in the Government.

national_raw_news.title: Ukraine, Russia exchange missile and drone strikes claiming 11 lives on both sides
national_raw_news.content: Ukraine and Russia exchanged missiles and drones today, with attacks killing at least 11 people on both sides. Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia in one of Kyiv’s largest aerial attacks of the war, killing six people. Five people were killed in Russia’s southwestern Rostov region after drone attacks targeted three towns. The strikes, involving more than 150 drones, also damaged several homes and a railway station and sparked a forest fire. An 83-year-old man was killed after a Ukrainian drone struck a private home in the Moscow region. Moscow’s Governor also confirmed that a Ukrainian attack triggered a fire at a Wildberries warehouse in Podolsk. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight. Meanwhile, Russian strikes killed five people in Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a missile attack on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and injured 14 others. Further strikes killed one person in Sumy and two in Zaporizhzhia. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it had targeted a metallurgical plant in Kryvyi Rih and several military-industrial facilities in Kyiv.

national_raw_news.title: Indonesia Declares 14-Day Emergency Response Period After 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake
national_raw_news.content: In Indonesia, a 14-day emergency response period was declared in East Nusa Tenggara province today after a powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Flores yesterday morning. According to a decree issued by East Nusa Tenggara Governor Melki Laka Lena, the emergency response will remain in effect till 28th of this month. The measure is intended to facilitate disaster response, evacuations, relief distribution and recovery efforts in the affected areas. Indonesia’s National Disaster Management Agency said the earthquake and 341 aftershocks had killed 51 people and injured 113 others. Hundreds of buildings across the region were also damaged. Several flights in East Nusa Tenggara were cancelled following the earthquake. Officials said people may still be trapped inside damaged buildings in several areas. Landslides have also been reported, with debris blocking roads and hampering rescue and relief operations.

national_raw_news.title: Category One Hurricane Lala hits Hawaii with strong winds and torrential rain
national_raw_news.content: Pacific island nation of Hawaii is facing strong winds and torrential rain as Category One Hurricane Lala moves across the Big Island. Lala has maximum sustained winds of around 120 kilometres per hour. Forecasters warn of up to 63 centimetres of rain, raising the risk of flash floods and mudslides. A hurricane warning is in effect for the Big Island. Tropical storm warnings cover Maui County, Oahu, Kauai and Ni’ihau. Officials have urged residents to remain indoors and avoid travelling. The National Hurricane Centre said Lala’s eyewall was reaching the southern Big Island. The storm is expected to move west across the island chain later today. Power outages have affected thousands of people on the island. Shelters have been opened, while officials warn of dangerous flooding, falling trees and strong winds. The storm could mark the Big Island’s first direct hurricane strike in more than 150 years.

While the women’s doubles duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will face Paula Lopez and Lucia Rodriguez of Spain in the first round. In the mixed doubles category, fifteenth seed pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto have also proceeded to the round of 32 after a bye.

national_raw_news.title: India Draw 2-2 With China in FIH Women’s Hockey World Cup Opener 16 Aug 2026 | 9:30 PM 87
national_raw_news.content: In the FIH Women’s Hockey World Cup, India began their campaign with a thrilling 2-2 draw against China in a group-stage match at Amstelveen in the Netherlands, today. Navneet gave India an early lead in the eighth minute, but China equalised through Zhang Ying’s penalty stroke in the 15th minute. Deepika restored India’s lead in the 25th minute with a penalty-corner goal. China fought back in the third quarter, with Ma Ning converting a penalty corner in the 39th minute to level the score at 2-2. India and China are in Pool D alongside England and South Africa. The top two teams from the pool will advance to the next round.

national_raw_news.title: Magnus Carlsen wins Esports World Cup chess title for second consecutive year 16 Aug 2026 | 7:48 AM 453
national_raw_news.content: In Chess, World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen has won Esports World Cup title for the second year in a row, by defeating Belarusian Grandmaster Denis Lazavik 2-0 in Paris, France. Representing Team Liquid, the 35-year-old Norwegian remained completely undefeated throughout the entire tournament. Meanwhile, American Grandmaster Hikaru Nakamura secured third place after defeating Alireza Firouzja 4-1 in a chaotic bronze-medal match that was repeatedly disrupted by technical problems and internet disconnections. The championship layout followed a best-of-three sets format, where the first two sets featured four games each, and a final two-game set was reserved as a tiebreaker if needed.

national_raw_news.title: FPIs Invest ₹16,621 Crore in Indian Equities So Far in August 16 Aug 2026 | 4:35 PM 88
national_raw_news.content: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have remained net buyers of Indian equities during the first two week of August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested 16,621 crore rupees in the domestic stock market so far this month. Of the total investment, 11,199 crore rupees came through purchases on the stock exchanges, while 5 thousand 422 crore rupees was invested through the primary market. The buying momentum, which gathered pace in July, has continued into August, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals and strong quarterly earnings. Meanwhile, buying interest was also seen in the debt market. So far in August, Foreign Portfolio Investors have invested 69 crore rupees in debt securities through the General Limit route. Through the Fully Accessible Route, FPIs have invested 972 crore rupees during the period under review.

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance DRI uncovers large-scale illegal use of SAFTA agreement in areca imports Months long investigation reveals defrauding exchequer of over Rs. 2,500 crore (approx.); Rs. 75 lakh cash, 160 MT areca nuts seized (approx.); Nine arrested Syndicates imported areca nuts into India from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries by mis-declaring country of origin as Bangladesh Licence of Customs Broker firm responsible for clearance of most of the fraudulent imports of areca nuts suspended प्रविष्टि तिथि: 16 AUG 2026 10:51AM by PIB Delhi The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), in a month-long intelligence-led operation, has dismantled a major network involved in importing South-East Asian areca nuts into India by falsely declaring them as Bangladeshi origin and fraudulently availing concessional duty benefits under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA). The investigation has so far revealed a potential revenue loss of more than Rs. 2,500 crore. Nine persons have been arrested in connection with the case. The import of areca nuts into India attracts a Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 100%. However, eligible imports of areca nuts made under SAFTA agreement are fully exempt from customs duty. The areca nuts originating from Bangladesh are entitled to exemption under SAFTA if imports meet the prescribed Rules of Origin criterion. Intelligence gathered and developed by DRI indicated that certain syndicates were fraudulently claiming the SAFTA benefits on a very large scale on imports of areca nuts. While they were importing areca nuts originating and sourced from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries, they were mis-declaring the country of origin of areca nuts imported into India as Bangladesh. Thereafter, simultaneous searches were conducted at multiple premises linked to importers, Customs Brokers and IEC holders in Kolkata and Visakhapatnam. Several incriminating documents and substantial evidences establishing the South-East Asian origin of Areca nuts were recovered. DRI officers also recovered and seized around Rs. 75 lakh in cash, believed to be sale proceeds of the illegally imported goods. A live consignment of around 160 MT of areca nuts. The investigations so far have revealed huge scale of fraudulent imports of areca nuts in which exchequer has been duped of customs duty in excess of Rs 2,500 crore in recent years. The masterminds were facilitating the import of areca nuts from South-East Asian countries into one of the EPZ in Bangladesh and thereafter routing the goods to India merely changing containers and bags and passing them off as Bangladeshi-origin areca nuts. They had fraudulently obtained SAFTA Certificates of Origin from Bangladeshi authorities. The masterminds were charging substantial commissions from Indian importers for arranging the routing, documentation, clearance and transportation of the consignments and massive collection of payments in cash... The investigation has also brought to light the use of hawala channels and dummy entities for movement and layering of the financial proceeds. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Civil Aviation Accidental Discharge of Licensed Weapon at Varanasi Airport प्रविष्टि तिथि: 16 AUG 2026 2:02PM by PIB Delhi On 16 August 2026, at approximately 0930 hours, a passenger, namely Shri Kamlesh Kedarnath Rai, scheduled to travel from Varanasi to Mumbai on Air India Express flight IX 1810 declared a licensed firearm (7.62 mm pistol with 21 live cartridges) at the check-in counter, as required under the prescribed procedure. The passenger was escorted to the designated screening area for completion of the mandatory security formalities. During the handling and inspection of the weapon, a round was accidentally discharged. The projectile ricocheted and caused injuries to two screening personnel, Shri Rohit Raj and Ms Suman Kumari. Both personnel were immediately provided assistance and shifted to New Lakshmi Trauma Center, Varanasi, for medical treatment. The local police were informed immediately and the passenger has been detained for investigation and further action in accordance with law. The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) is examining the circumstances leading to the incident, including adherence to the prescribed procedures for handling and carriage of licensed weapons at airports. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings. Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), under the Union Ministry of Finance, has dismantled a major smuggling network accused of illegally importing areca nuts from South-East Asia while falsely declaring them as Bangladeshi-origin goods to exploit concessional duty benefits under the South Asian Free Trade Area agreement (SAFTA). The month-long operation has revealed a potential revenue loss exceeding Rs 2,500 crore to the exchequer, with nine individuals arrested in connection with the case. Syndicates imported areca nuts from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian nations, then fraudulently claimed full customs duty exemption available under SAFTA. Areca nut imports into India normally attract a Basic Customs Duty of 100 per cent, but eligible imports from Bangladesh receive complete exemption provided they meet prescribed Rules of Origin criteria. The investigation revealed that networks routed areca nuts through an Export Processing Zone in Bangladesh, where goods were transferred into different containers and bags before being dispatched to India. The syndicates fraudulently obtained Certificates of Origin from Bangladeshi authorities to support false declarations and claim SAFTA benefits, with masterminds charging substantial commissions from Indian importers for arranging routing, documentation and clearance. DRI officers carried out simultaneous searches at locations linked to importers, customs brokers and Importer Exporter Code holders in Kolkata and Visakhapatnam. Authorities seized approximately Rs 75 lakh in cash and about 160 metric tonnes of areca nuts during the operation. The licence of a customs broker firm responsible for clearing most fraudulent imports has been suspended. Further, nine persons have been arrested so far in connection with the case. The investigation has so far revealed a potential revenue loss of more than Rs 2,500 crore to the exchequer, while nine persons have been arrested in connection with the case. According to the Ministry, syndicates were importing areca nuts into India from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other Southeast Asian countries and falsely declaring Bangladesh as the country of origin to fraudulently avail concessional duty benefits under SAFTA. The DRI dismantled the network following a month-long intelligence-led operation. Areca nut imports into India attract a Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 100 per cent. However, eligible areca nuts originating from Bangladesh are fully exempt from customs duty under SAFTA, provided the imports meet the prescribed Rules of Origin criteria. According to the Ministry, the syndicates falsely declared the areca nuts as originating from Bangladesh to fraudulently avail duty benefits under SAFTA, with the investigation so far revealing a potential revenue loss of more than Rs 2,500 crore." As part of the operation, authorities have seized approximately Rs 75 lakh in cash and about 160 metric tonnes of areca nuts. The Ministry said the licence of a Customs Broker firm responsible for the clearance of most of the fraudulent areca nut imports has also been suspended. The case centres on misuse of the preferential tariff framework under SAFTA, which provides customs duty concessions to eligible goods originating from member countries subject to compliance with prescribed origin rules. The DRI, the country's apex anti-smuggling intelligence and enforcement agency under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), investigates cases involving customs duty evasion, commercial fraud and smuggling. national_raw_news.content: Amrit Udyan opens for public visit for summer annuals edition 2026 Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Amrit Udyan opens for public visit for summer annuals edition 2026 ANI | Updated: Aug 16, 2026 14:44 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 16 (ANI): Amrit Udyan in Rashtrapati Bhavan has opened for public visit for the Amrit Udyan Summer Annuals Edition, 2026. It will remain open till September 15 this year. President Droupadi Murmu had graced the opening of Amrit Udyan Summer Annuals Edition on Thursday. The Udyan will remain open from 10 am to 6 pm, with the last entry at 5 pm. It will remain closed on all Mondays for maintenance. An official release said that entry and exit for visitors will be from Gate No. 35, located near North Avenue Road. Entry to Amrit Udyan will be free of cost. Visitors have to book their slots online at visit.rashtrapatibhavan.gov.in advance. Booking of slots for a particular day will close at 10 am on the previous day. On-the-spot booking is not available. For the convenience of the visitors, drinking water stalls, first aid posts, rain shelter and restrooms will be set up along the route of the visit. A shuttle bus service will also be available from Central Secretariat Metro Station to the entry point to the Amrit Udyan at an interval of every 30 minutes between 9.30 am and 6 pm.
